text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Oil Minister Isa al-Mazeedi says 30 roadside petrol stations to be privatised soon. The move was first announced last year as part of a government plan to shed its holdings in some 60 local companies.
- Parliament is expected to pass a law lifting restrictions on the launch of new newspapers.

- An academic study ordered by Washington proposes granting residencies to 519,000 Palestinians to live in Kuwait and other Arab states to resolve the refugee problem as part of Israeli- Palestinian final status peace talks. Some of Kuwait's 400,000- strong Palestinian community fled during Iraq's 1990-91 occupation, others were later expelled amid hostility from Kuwaitis who accused them of collaborating with Iraqi forces.
- Jordan-Kuwait Bank asks Kuwaiti clients to check their accounts. The Amman-based bank says some Kuwaiti depositors have not contacted the bank in 15 years and could risk loosing their funds.

- MP submits proposal to scrap a salary cap for expatriates to allow them to bring their families to Kuwait to revive the local economy. Foreigners earning less than 450 dinars ($1,500) in the public sector and 650 dinars ($2,150) in the private sector are not allowed family residencies.
